formatting.fileFormat: Word document; PDF is not accepted. 'For submission and review, please submit the manuscript as a Word document. Do not submit your manuscript in PDF format.'
formatting.margins: Right margins unjustified (ragged); no margin width is stated
formatting.pageNumbers: Start each section (title page, abstract, text, references, figure legends, tables) on a new page, numbered consecutively, beginning with the title page
formatting.referenceStyle: AMA Manual of Style, 11th edition (and/or ICMJE Recommendations). Number references in the order they appear in the text, do not alphabetize; cite with superscript arabic numerals in text, tables, and legends; list all authors up to 6, if more than 6 list the first 3 followed by et al; include the issue number in parentheses after the volume; AI/LLM tools must not be used to generate or format references
formatting.coverLetter: Required. 'Include a cover letter and complete contact information for the corresponding author (affiliation, postal/mail address, email address, and telephone number) and whether the authors have published, posted, or submitted any related papers from the same study.'
formatting.supplement: Online-only material is submitted as a single Word document with pages numbered consecutively; elements are numbered in order of citation as eTable 1, eTable 2, eFigure 1, eFigure 2, eMethods, and each must be cited in the main text; a list of elements on the first page; text in Arial 10 pt single-spaced, main heading 12 pt bold, subheadings 10 pt bold; table titles Arial 12 pt bold, footnotes 8 pt; figure titles Arial 12 pt bold, legends 8 pt; supplementary references in a separate section; material must be important to the understanding of the report and must not repeat the main article; the journal is not a data repository (large data sets go to public repositories)
formatting.titlePage: First page of the manuscript file: manuscript title; full names, highest academic degrees, and affiliations of all authors (new affiliation also listed if changed since the work was done); name and complete contact information for the corresponding author; manuscript word count (not including title, abstract, acknowledgment, references, tables, and figure legends)

headings: Intervention(s) (for clinical trials) or Exposure(s) (for observational studies)

abstracts.other: Narrative Review is NOT a JAMA Dermatology article type (the Narrative Review rows are coded 'Exclude: DER' and the Reviews section says 'The journal will consider 1 type of review article'); the 300-word 3-part abstract block is on the page under the heading 'Abstracts for Narrative Reviews or Special Communications'. Meta-analysis abstracts: no more than 350 words with headings Importance, Objective, Data Sources, Study Selection, Data Extraction and Synthesis, Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s), Results, Conclusions and Relevance. 'Include a structured abstract for reports of original data, meta-analyses, and systematic reviews.' 'Abstracts are not required for Editorials, Viewpoints, and special features.' 'No information should be reported in the abstract that does not appear in the text of the manuscript.' Design, Setting, and Participants must be kept as separate headings at submission. Summary demographic information and the number of participants go in the first sentence of the abstract Results. For clinical trials the registry name, registration number, and URL must be listed at the end of the abstract. Consensus Statements require a structured abstract but the page gives no heading list for them on this journal's page. Special Communications: two abstract headings mention them (350-word systematic-review style and 300-word 3-part style) and no sentence resolves which applies.

keyPoints.rules: 'Limit this section to 75-100 words or less.' Required only for research and review manuscripts; placed as a separate section called Key Points before the Abstract. Question: focused question based on the study hypothesis or goal/purpose, limit to 1 sentence. Findings: results of the study/review including the design, can include 1 to 2 sentences, report basic numbers only and state whether results are statistically significant, do not include results of statistical tests or measures of variance, do not emphasize secondary outcomes. Meaning: key conclusion and implication based on the primary finding(s), limit to 1 sentence. For Systematic Reviews: 'Limit to no more than 100 words. This is different from the Abstract.' Not used for Research Letters.

journalNotes: The page is a JAMA Network multi-journal template whose Include/Exclude/Comments lines are visible in the text; article types coded for other journals (Narrative Review, Clinical Challenge, Images in Neurology, Cardiovascular Images, From the Heart, On the Brain, etc.) are not included here. A 'Clinical Challenge' heading does appear on the page but its Include line excludes DER; the Dermatology variant is the Clinicopathological Challenge.

Brief Report: a template label 'Include: DER / Comments: Brief Report' exists, but no Brief Report row, paragraph, or limits (no 'Recommended length', '1200 words', or '15 references') appear anywhere on the JAMA Dermatology page, so it is not listed as a type here.

Notable Notes and Dermatology Patient Page do not appear anywhere on the page. Editorials and Invited Commentaries are not listed as submission types (only 'Abstracts are not required for Editorials, Viewpoints, and special features').
Reviews: 'The journal will consider 1 type of review article' (Systematic Review without meta-analysis); Narrative Review rows are coded Exclude: DER. Consensus Statement is a DER-specific type.

Clinical Trial and Meta-analysis are study types under Original Investigation (with their own paragraphs, subtitles, abstract headings, and checklists); Other Observational Studies share the Original Investigation limits (3000 words, 5 tables/figures, 50-75 references, 3 Key Points).

Title limit: 100 characters (including spaces) for reports of research and other major articles; 60 characters for shorter article types such as opinion articles and Letters and for subtitles to major articles. Include the study type as a subtitle only for clinical trials, meta-analyses, and systematic reviews. Avoid overly general or declarative titles, titles stating the direction of results, questions as titles, and abbreviations in the title or abstract.

Recommended file sizes: individual files no more than 500 kB and not exceeding 1 MB; all files together not exceeding 5 MB (excluding video). Figures are uploaded as separate files (1 file per figure), not embedded in the manuscript; tables go at the end of the manuscript file and must not be images.

Tables: brief title preferably no longer than 10 to 15 words; single-spaced 10- or 12-point font; minimum 2 columns; superscript letter footnotes; report frequencies as No. (%); no decimal places in percentages if the sample size is less than 100. Figures: titles preferably 10-15 words; no more than 4 panels unless justified; no pie charts, 3-D graphs, or stacked bar charts; resolution >=350 ppi for photographs/illustrations and >=600 ppi for line drawings; generally no larger than 1 MB each; labeled images submitted with and without markers; AI-created or manipulated clinical images not permitted.

Video: .mov, .wmv, .mpg, .mpeg, .mp4, or .avi; max 25 MB at initial submission; preferred length 5 minutes or less; title max 100 characters; caption 1-5 sentences; description 3-10 sentences; Patient Permission form for identifiable patients; blurring or masking faces is not permitted. Audio: .mp3, .wav, or .aiff; max 25 MB; max 5 minutes.

Acknowledgment section must include author contributions, a data access statement from at least 1 and no more than 2 named authors using the exact wording 'had full access to all the data in the study and takes responsibility for the integrity of the data and the accuracy of the data analysis', conflict of interest disclosures (3 years before submission, regardless of amount or value), funding and the role of the funder, and a Data Sharing Statement for all reports of research. Any AI use in manuscript preparation must be reported there (tool name, version, manufacturer, dates of use). The Group Authorship paragraph is coded 'All journals except DER and OTO'.

Patient identification: a signed statement of informed consent to publish patient descriptions, photographs, video, and pedigrees must be obtained from identifiable persons; do not submit masked photographs; black bars across the eyes are not acceptable; patients' initials or other identifiers must not appear in images. The Patient Permission form is available in Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, and Spanish on request.

Authorship: all authors complete an electronic Authorship Form and Publishing Agreement; ICMJE 4 criteria; no more than 2 co-corresponding authors; AI tools do not qualify for authorship. The journal uses single-anonymized peer review; accepted articles are generally published Online First and then in a print/online issue; research articles become free access 12 months after publication; optional CC-BY-NC-ND or CC-BY open access for $6000.
unread: All character ranges of the page (0-229834) were fetched in overlapping slices. The raw HTML could not be downloaded directly (HTTP 403), so extraction went through WebFetch's summarizer, which caps each verbatim quote at 125 characters; quotes are therefore sentence fragments, and minor non-numeric rules may have been condensed.
